description: ASTRA-X: Galactic Rescue is an educational space adventure game developed using the Scratch platform. This game takes place in the year 2048, where players take on the role of a Commander leading a mission to rescue astronauts stranded in outer space. Players must select a suitable spacecraft, avoid asteroids and space debris, and complete three exciting challenges on Mars, Jupiter and Saturn. Throughout the mission, players will also face NASA IQ questions and solve various puzzles to activate the rescue system. This project combines entertainment, science and technology to create an interactive learning experience while improving players' critical thinking, decision-making and problem-solving skills, as well as encouraging interest in space exploration and STEM education.
summary:
ASTRA-X: Galactic Rescue is an educational space adventure game developed using the Scratch platform. This game aims to increase players' interest in science, technology and space exploration while developing critical thinking, decision-making and problem-solving skills.
Set in the year 2048, players take on the role of a Commander leading a mission to rescue a group of astronauts stranded in outer space due to a damaged spacecraft. Players must select a suitable spacecraft, avoid asteroids and space debris, and complete three main challenges on Mars, Jupiter and Saturn. In addition, players must answer NASA IQ questions and solve puzzles involving number sequences, circuit connections and symbol matching to activate the rescue system.
In conclusion, ASTRA-X combines entertainment and education through interactive gameplay. It provides an opportunity to improve knowledge of space science while encouraging younger generations to develop an interest in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM).
details:
Game Workflow (7-Step Rescue Mission)

Prologue & Mode Selection: Players enter their Commander callsign and choose Single Player (Global Leaderboard), Join Room (compete with up to 40 players), or Create Room (Host) (play & compete, or wait in Host Spectator Mode watching the live leaderboard).

Step 1 – Spacecraft Selection: Choose between ORION (95% Speed, 60% Durability, 55% Shield), VOYAGER 1 (55% Speed, 95% Durability, 95% Shield), or APOLLO 11 (80% Balanced).

Step 2 – NASA Launchpad 39A & Earth Ascent: Experience an ignition cutscene with synthesized rocket audio and radio voice comms, then pilot the spacecraft through atmospheric clouds and green target rings to reach 200 km outer space.

Step 3 – Deep Space Asteroid & Debris Belt: Survive a 42-second debris field of tumbling asteroids and space junk while collecting 5 glowing NASA Satellites to restore shields and durability.

Step 4 – Multi-Planet Challenges (Mars → Jupiter → Saturn):

Planet 1 – Mars (Round-Globe Rover Survival): Drive a 6-wheeled rover across a 3D spherical Mars terrain using a floating 3D navigation arrow and radar to collect Oxygen, Battery, and Water, avoiding craters, rocks, and dust storms before returning to Mars Base.

Planet 2 – Jupiter (Cosmic Navigation): Navigate Jupiter’s corridor, collect 8 Energy Cells, avoid glowing Red Radiation-Danger Zones, and fly through the Research Checkpoint.

Planet 3 – Saturn (Gas Giant Boss Battle): Fight KRONOS-OMEGA (600 HP) inside Saturn’s swirling ammonia clouds, targeting its 3 glowing cores while dodging its 5-way enraged plasma barrage.

Step 5 – Walkable 3D Destroyed Shuttle & Rescue Puzzles: Walk a 3D astronaut through 3 ruined shuttle bays (Airlock Bay, Engineering Bay, and Crew Cabin) to solve 9 randomized STEM questions (3 per room drawn from a 30-question pool covering Code Sequences, Circuit Connections, and Space Symbols & Systems), followed by a 15-second tractor-beam escape cutscene.

Step 6 & 7 – Extra IQ Briefing & Final Leaderboard: Explore 6 NASA mission briefings (Orion, Voyager 1, Apollo 11, Perseverance/MOXIE, Juno, Cassini-Huygens), view your 100-point Mission Breakdown, earn a Commander Rank (Rookie, Skilled, Elite, or Legendary Commander), and compare scores on the Global or 40-Player Room Leaderboard.

How It Works — Gameplay & Technical Innovations

Ship Durability & NASA IQ Challenge System

Instead of traditional "lives," ASTRA-X uses Shield and Durability bars. When durability drops to 0%, the game pauses and triggers a NASA IQ Challenge drawn randomly from a 30-question science bank:

  • Answering restores durability to 50% so players can continue.
  • Correct answer: +10 pts | Incorrect answer: -5 pts
2. Spherical 3D Rover Physics on Mars

Rather than a flat 2D plane, the Mars mission places the rover, Mars Base, supplies, rocks, craters, and dust storms directly on a 3D sphere (MARS_R = 24). Vector projection keeps the rover aligned to the sphere’s surface normal while a 3D floating arrow and top-right radar guide the player around the globe.

3. 40-Player Multiplayer Rooms & Host Spectator Mode

Built on Firebase Realtime Database, teachers, event hosts, or friends can create a 6-character Room Code supporting up to 40 players simultaneously:

  • Invite Link: ?room=XXXXXX automatically pre-fills the room code for players.
  • Host Flexibility: The host can either Play & Compete or stay on the Live Auto-Refreshing Leaderboard (updates every 3 seconds) to monitor all participants’ status (Playing / Finished), ship choice, time, and score.
4. Cross-Platform Controls & Synthesized Audio
  • Supports PC (Arrow Keys / WASD + Spacebar) and Phone/Tablet Landscape (responsive 100dvh 3:2 viewport scaling with virtual touch joystick and Fire Laser button).
  • Zero external audio files: All background music tracks, laser shots, alarms, rocket roar, and radio voice synthesis are generated dynamically via the Web Audio API and SpeechSynthesis API.

Game Objectives & Educational Outcomes

Main Objective

Complete the rescue mission from Earth to Saturn by surviving deep-space hazards, overcoming three planetary challenges, and solving logic and electrical-circuit puzzles to rescue the stranded astronauts.

Educational Objectives & Learning Outcomes

  1. Enhance Space Science Knowledge: Teach real facts about Mars (iron oxide, MOXIE oxygen production), Jupiter (Juno mission, radiation belts), Saturn (Cassini-Huygens, rings), and historic NASA spacecraft (Orion, Voyager 1, Apollo 11).
  2. Develop Critical Thinking: Encourage strategic trade-offs when choosing spacecraft attributes (speed vs. durability/shield) and managing energy/durability under pressure.
  3. Strengthen STEM Problem-Solving: Reinforce number sequences, closed vs. open electrical circuits, solar photovoltaic conversion, and spacecraft instrumentation.
  4. Distinguish Fact from Fiction: Explicitly separate real NASA science (e.g., Perseverance, Juno, Cassini) from fictional arcade mechanics (e.g., power cores, boss battles) inside the quiz feedback and briefings.
